messages.subject: Break in cut function?
parts:
Hi all,

I want to separate dates by three months.

> head(date)
               [1] "2000-01-01" "2000-01-02" "2000-01-03" 
 > str(date)
           Date[1:240], format: "2000-01-01" "2000-01-02" "2000-01-03"  ...

  ind <- cut(date, breaks='3 months') 

"Cut" here will start from jan and do this  Jan Feb Mar    Apr May Jun etc….
  
How to force cut to start from December  and consider three months as 
Dec Jan Feb
 Mar Apr May etc ….. 
 
Thanks,
bic

messages.author: 6eb170ca555d9bdd
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Break in cut function?
parts:
This is admittedly not the most elegant solution, but assuming your dates come in an uninterrupted sequence from Jan - December, one approach might be to ignore the first two months, which would include the previous December, and begin your cut on '2000-03-01'.

# subset date to include only March, 2000 onwards
new_dates <- date[ i : nrow(date) ]  # where i = the index of '2000-03-01'.

# apply the cut
ind <- cut( new_dates, breaks = '3 months')


I hope that solution works for what you're trying to accomplish. 

Best,
Rich

messages.author: f14d4c9d01f43388
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Break in cut function?
parts:
Hi

I would do it this way: just create a "reference" data-set with the quarter you want, and which value you want to associate to it, then match this with the month extracted from your date.

# Your data:
dates_chr <- paste("2000-01-", 1:12, sep="")
dates_dat <- as.Date(dates_chr, "%Y-%d-%m")

## ref dataset:
df <- data.frame(Q=paste("Q", 1:4, sep=""), M=c(2:12,1))

## merge/match:
df[match(as.numeric(format(dates_dat, "%m")), df$M),"Q"]

And if you fancy the tidyverse package, code would be:

library(tidyverse)
data_frame(dates_chr=paste("2000-01-", 1:12, sep="")) %>%
  mutate(dates_dat = as.Date(dates_chr, "%Y-%d-%m"),
         dates_mon=as.numeric(format(dates_dat, "%m"))) %>%
  left_join(df, by=c("dates_mon"="M"))

    dates_chr  dates_dat dates_mon      Q
        <chr>     <date>     <dbl> <fctr>
 1  2000-01-1 2000-01-01         1     Q4
 2  2000-01-2 2000-02-01         2     Q1
 3  2000-01-3 2000-03-01         3     Q2


Best,

Matthieu
